# E04: Continental separation and the western margin

**Window:** Mesozoic–early Cenozoic research frame; chronology to be resolved by process.

**Question:** Which rifting, separation and magmatic episodes affected the ancestors of today’s territory?

## Evidence presently available in this seed

The west-coast tectono-magmatic paper is relevant to a multi-stage margin history. It does not justify treating the western margin, Ghats and present beach as one simultaneous creation.

Source routes: [S004](../sources/S004.md), [S005](../sources/S005.md).

## What this does not establish

The earlier outline’s 250-million-year division was editorial, not a dated local event. Exact India–Madagascar separation and later spreading ages have not been verified in this seed.

## Research tasks

- [ ] Retrieve regional plate-kinematic and geochronological studies.
- [ ] Record separate dates for rift initiation, final separation, seafloor spreading, volcanism and later deformation.
- [ ] Mark adjacent offshore observations as explanatory context.
- [ ] Avoid assigning modern continental outlines to all palaeogeographic maps.
